text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.74% today to $139.48, extending a two-week decline of 3.4%. The decline came as oil prices softened slightly—U.S. crude dropped to $89.62 per barrel today—despite significant geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran's reported attacks on U.S. military sites in Kuwait and the IEA's warning about disrupted confidence in the Strait of Hormuz should theoretically support oil prices, but markets may be pricing in uncertainty about whether these tensions will actually disrupt supply flows, or reflecting broader economic concerns signaled by record UK diesel prices driving inflation higher.

The stock has been volatile over the past week, swinging from $135.59 to a peak of $142.28 before retreating. Oil majors often trade on a combination of crude prices and investor sentiment about global economic health; softer oil prices paired with signs of inflation pressures abroad may be creating conflicting signals about demand.
